stories.title: Apply for an exemption from Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
stories.summary: HMRC published new guidance today on how sole traders and landlords can apply for exemptions from the mandatory Making Tax Digital for Income Tax requirements, including criteria for digital exclusion.

stories.title: 436,000 sole traders and landlords make their tax digital
stories.summary: Over 436,000 sole traders and landlords have successfully submitted their first MTD for Income Tax quarterly update for 2026-27, with over 570,000 now signed up. HMRC will begin mandatorily enrolling remaining eligible customers from September 2026.

stories.title: Asylum appeals target launched for faster removals
stories.summary: The Home Office introduced a new 24-week target for asylum and immigration appeal decisions, aiming to reduce the current average wait of 67 weeks. Expected to save taxpayers an estimated £6.9 billion and speed up deportations of those with no right to remain.

stories.title: UK condemns Houthi escalation at UN Security Council on Yemen
stories.summary: UK Ambassador Kate Foster called for Iran to cease support for the Houthis following drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, attacks on Red Sea shipping, and violations of Yemeni airspace. Over 22 million Yemenis require humanitarian assistance, including 18 million facing food insecurity.

stories.title: UK continues crackdown on Russia with tough new sanctions
stories.summary: New Russia sanctions were announced by the Foreign Secretary as the UK continues targeted economic pressure on Russia. The sanctions are part of a joint statement with allied countries.

stories.title: Millions to receive essential benefit payments early
stories.summary: DWP confirmed benefit payments originally due 31 August will be brought forward to Friday 28 August ahead of the August bank holiday weekend. This affects Universal Credit, State Pension, PIP, Attendance Allowance, Carer's Allowance, DLA and other major benefits.

stories.title: Help ramped up amid UK's 'worst' bluetongue outbreak
stories.summary: With 395 bluetongue virus cases confirmed across the UK—described by the chief vet as 'absolutely the worst' outbreak ever—DEFRA is ramping up testing and support. Farmers are urgently urged to vaccinate livestock before the projected peak in cases driven by the ongoing hot weather.

stories.title: Just 20 of 6,600 Defra staff working on climate adaptation amid drought and wildfires
stories.summary: An investigation by The Guardian reveals that only 20 of DEFRA's 6,600 staff are dedicated to climate adaptation work, despite the ongoing drought and wildfire risk across England. Critics say this is a serious mismatch given the scale of climate-related challenges facing UK agriculture and rural communities.

stories.title: MoD says wind farm could weaken UK air defences
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence has formally objected to proposals for a wind farm in East Yorkshire, stating the turbines would interfere with air defence radar at RRH Staxton Wold and pose a physical obstruction to low-flying RAF and US Air Force aircraft conducting training exercises.

stories.title: Serious failings found in new military crimes unit, leaked report finds
stories.summary: A leaked internal review reveals serious failings within the Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC), the new unit set up to independently investigate rape, sexual offences, murder and manslaughter within the military, raising concerns about whether victims are being adequately protected.

stories.title: Review launched to shape pathway to reach zero emission driving by 2035
stories.summary: BIST and the Department for Transport launched a ZEV Mandate review consultation open until 23 October 2026. Industry, manufacturers and consumers are invited to shape the pathway to 100% zero-emission new car and van sales by 2035. More than 1 in 4 new cars sold are now electric, with EV sales up 45% on July last year.

stories.title: Walk-in mental health centres to open in banks and libraries across England
stories.summary: The government announced plans for nearly 200 community mental health centres and dedicated mental health A&Es by 2029, backed by £343m. The first sites will open this autumn, with hubs planned for high-street locations like banks and libraries to give people experiencing mental health crises easier access to specialist care.

stories.title: Millions in England face longer waits for mental health care as NHS providers plan cuts
stories.summary: Multiple NHS mental health trusts are planning significant service and job cuts to balance their books, with East London Foundation Trust alone planning £25m in cuts. Millions of patients could face longer waits for mental health care as a result of the NHS-wide drive to balance budgets.

stories.title: Royal Mail raises prices for bulk users by a third
stories.summary: Royal Mail announced an average 25% price increase for bulk mail users — including NHS trusts sending medical appointment letters — from 5 October 2026. The price rise has been described as a blow to public sector organisations reliant on postal communications.
